_comment: Pin data for scripts/matrix_tool.py. 'pins' = recommended matrix pins in suggested order (edge pins first). 'extra' = usable but awkward (bottom pads, NFC). 'reserved' = do not use. 'split_link' = suggested half-duplex TRRS pin for a wired split (same on both halves); it is removed from the matrix pool when --split is used. Set verified:false where the pin map could not be confirmed against a manufacturer source. 'led_supply' = where per-key LED + and − connect.

rp2040_zero.label: Waveshare RP2040-Zero
rp2040_zero.notes: 20 castellated edge GPIOs (GP0-15, GP26-29). GP17-25 are small pads on the underside: usable, harder to solder. No SWD broken out. Not 5 V tolerant.

rp2040_tiny.label: Waveshare RP2040-Tiny
rp2040_tiny.notes: 20 castellated GPIOs, verified against Waveshare's pinout image (wiki RP2040-Tiny, 2026-10): right edge GP0-GP9, bottom GP10-GP13, left GP14, GP15, GP26-GP29. GP16 = onboard WS2812. GP24/GP25 sit on the 'user mode selection' pads (not edge pins). The main board has no buttons: BOOT and RESET are on the USB-C adapter board, joined by an 8-pin FPC cable.

rp2040_plus.label: Waveshare RP2040-Plus / Raspberry Pi Pico (Pico pinout)

reserved.GP29: VSYS/3 voltage sense (ADC3), not on header

rp2040_plus.notes: 26 header GPIOs. GP23/24/25/29 are wired to board functions and not on the header. Pico W variants use these for the wireless chip.

pico.label: Raspberry Pi Pico (RP2040)

reserved.GP29: VSYS/3 voltage sense (ADC3), not on header

pico.notes: Same 26 header GPIOs as the RP2040-Plus (GP0-22, GP26-28). GP23 = SMPS mode, GP24 = VBUS sense, GP25 = LED, GP29 = VSYS/3 sense: internal, not on the header. Only a BOOTSEL button, no RESET button (RUN is header pin 30: short it to GND to reset). Pico W: same keyboard pins; its LED is on the Wi-Fi chip. Pico 2 / 2 W are RP2350: not supported by QMK/Vial (2026-10).

pro_micro.label: Pro Micro (ATmega32U4, 5 V)
pro_micro.notes: 18 GPIOs. D0/D1 = I2C SDA/SCL (needed for OLEDs or I2C split). SOFT_SERIAL_PIN must be an INT pin: D0-D3 (D2 is the common choice; D0 on many boards). Elite-C/clones expose extra pins (B7, D5, C7, F1, F0).

nice_nano_v2.label: nice!nano v2 (nRF52840) and Pro-Micro-pinout clones (SuperMini nRF52840)
nice_nano_v2.notes: ZMK only. Matches ZMK's pro_micro gpio-map (positions 0-10,14-16,18-21). P0.09/P0.10 are NFC pins (pro_micro 10/16): usable as GPIO but use them last. P1.01/P1.02/P1.07 are inner pads, low-frequency I/O only. Wireless splits need no link pin. Clones share the edge pinout but often differ in pads, charging current and power switch — check the seller's diagram.
